- Challenge volume, response capacity, and unanswered-challenge age are tracked and reported together.
- A sustained congestion breach triggers a recorded resourcing decision or a recorded scope reduction, never a narrowing of standing.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/challenge-load-ledger
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-23)
- The challenge dashboard shows volume against capacity, not volume alone.
- Clock breaches surface as capacity events in the same tooling as operational incidents.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-23)
[ ] The ledger reports volume, capacity, and age as a series.
[ ] Each recorded congestion breach links to a resourcing or scope decision.
[ ] No eligibility criterion was changed in the same review window as a congestion breach without a recorded rationale.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-23)
Trigger review when unanswered-challenge age crosses the published threshold, or when standing or admissibility was narrowed within a window where congestion was breached.

artifacts.name: Challenge load ledger
artifacts.purpose: Volume, response capacity, unanswered-challenge age, and the decisions each breach produced.

artifacts.name: Congestion decision log
artifacts.purpose: For each breach: resourcing, scope reduction, or error-reduction chosen, with the record behind it.

artifacts.name: Standing-stability note
artifacts.purpose: Evidence that eligibility and admissibility were not adjusted in response to volume.

example.title: The queue that funded its own reviewers
example.description: Appeals against an automated denial triple after a model change. The ledger breaches its threshold, and the recorded decision is two additional funded reviewers and a scope reduction on the denial class — not an admissibility bar. The standing register is unchanged; the model change is reconsidered under its policy review trigger.

antiPatterns.title: Congestion as nuisance
antiPatterns.failure: Volume is treated as bad-faith filing, and the response is higher bars, longer clocks, or narrower eligibility.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Volume is read as a capacity signal and answered with resourcing or scope decisions on the record.
antiPatterns.warning: Bad-faith volume exists; filter it per case through admissibility, never through the standing register.

antiPatterns.title: The invisible queue
antiPatterns.failure: Challenges age silently because nothing reports unanswered age, so the system's own records hide the saturation.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Unanswered-challenge age is a first-class metric with a breach threshold.
antiPatterns.warning: A dashboard that shows only throughput hides the queue; report what has not been answered.

entries.title: MEC-24 Rescue register
entries.summary: Record every failure a person caught before it reached someone else, so near-misses become evidence about the condition rather than silence in the incident count.
cues: Count a caught failure as an occurrence with a cause, not as an absence of incidents.
Ask who caught it, what it cost them, and whether the condition is still there.
Treat repeat rescues against one unfixed condition as the strongest signal the register holds.
steps: Define what counts as a rescue: a failure that occurred, that the system or process would not have caught, and that a person caught before it reached anyone else.
Capture the near-miss condition, the person who caught it, the labor spent catching it, and whether the source condition was subsequently fixed.
Report rescues and incidents as one series. A falling incident count alongside a rising rescue count means the system is unchanged and the luck is not.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-24 Rescue register)
- Failures caught by a person before reaching anyone else are recorded as occurrences.
- Each rescue record names the near-miss condition and whether the source condition was fixed.
- Rescue counts and incident counts are reviewed together, never separately.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/rescue-register
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-24)
- The rescue register is an artifact in the human impact safety case.
- A rescue record cannot be closed without either a fix or a recorded decision not to fix.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-24)
[ ] Rescue records exist for the review period.
[ ] Each names the near-miss condition and the labor spent catching it.
[ ] Repeat rescues against one unfixed condition appear as a standing item.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-24)
Trigger review when rescues rise while incidents fall, or when the same condition is rescued more than once.

artifacts.name: Rescue register
artifacts.purpose: One row per caught failure: near-miss condition, catcher, labor spent, and whether the source was fixed.

artifacts.name: Repeat-condition list
artifacts.purpose: Conditions that have produced more than one rescue, with the decision taken on each.

artifacts.name: Rescue and incident series
artifacts.purpose: Both counts on one axis, so a falling incident count cannot hide a rising one.

example.title: Zero incidents, three hundred rescues
example.description: A medication reconciliation defect produces no incidents for a year because nurses catch every mismatch before dispensing. The register shows 300 rescues against the same unfixed interface, 4,000 hours of checking nobody rostered, and an interface the institution decided not to change. The incident count reads zero. The register reads a system held together by people.

antiPatterns.title: The lucky safety record
antiPatterns.failure: A clean incident log is read as a safe system, while the rescues that produced the clean log go unrecorded.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Rescues and incidents are one series, and the register is part of the safety case.
antiPatterns.warning: A falling incident count is good news only when rescues are flat too.

antiPatterns.title: Hero accounting
antiPatterns.failure: Regular rescues against one unfixed condition are praised as reliable staff rather than read as a defect in the condition.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: A repeat rescue is a standing item against the condition, owned by whoever controls it.
antiPatterns.warning: Reliability of the person is evidence about the system, not about the person.

entries.title: MEC-25 Procurement stress test
entries.summary: Evaluate a candidate system before money moves by making frontline personnel run adversarial scenarios, with hard disqualifiers that outrank any composite score.
cues: Run live scenarios against dirty data instead of accepting a scripted demo.
Record the labor the evaluation itself consumes, and who is pulled from duty to spend it.
Let the people who observe a disqualifier trigger it, not a committee that reviews their notes.
steps: Write the scenarios before choosing among vendors, with the failure modes the system is expected to absorb, and keep a rotating variant set for each session.
State each pass threshold with its evidence, who set it, and its review condition; a number that cannot say why it is the number is a line drawn to fit the answer.
Declare what the evaluation costs: which staff, how long, who covers their duties, and what happens to the finding when the unit cannot spare them.
Run each redline as a decision by whoever observed it, with the recording requirement from MEC-24: an occurrence, the labor it cost, and whether the vendor dispute changes the finding.
Bind every projection the evaluation produces to a post-deployment measurement of the same quantity, with a review condition that reopens the admission when they diverge.
entries.policyRequirement:
Policy requirement (MEC-25 Procurement stress test)
- A candidate system is evaluated through live adversarial scenarios run by frontline personnel, not through vendor-controlled demonstrations.
- Disqualifier findings recorded by the personnel who observed them trigger the disqualification; a committee may not downgrade an observed occurrence without a recorded reason.
- Every threshold in the evaluation carries its justification, its author, and a review condition.
- The evaluation states the labor it consumes and who bears it.
- Projections made at evaluation time are bound to post-deployment measurement by a review condition.
Reference: https://ethotechnics.org/mechanisms/patterns/procurement-stress-test
entries.productRequirement:
Product requirement (MEC-25)
- The vendor receives the scenario classes, not the scenario contents, and the rotating set is held by the evaluator.
- An evaluation artifact records each occurrence observed, the labor spent observing it, and the disqualifier decision.
entries.auditEvidenceChecklist:
Audit evidence checklist (MEC-25)
[ ] Scenario set exists, with authorship dates preceding vendor shortlisting.
[ ] Each threshold carries its evidence and a named author.
[ ] Evaluation labor is stated: roles, duration, backfill.
[ ] Redline findings are recorded by observers, not summarized by committee.
[ ] Every projection has a named post-deployment counterpart and review condition.
entries.postmortemTrigger:
Postmortem trigger (MEC-25)
Trigger review when a system admitted through the evaluation shows a burden pattern the evaluation projected would not occur, or when a redline finding was downgraded without a recorded reason.

artifacts.name: Scenario set and rotation record
artifacts.purpose: The adversarial scenarios, their authors, dates, and which variant each session used.

artifacts.name: Threshold register
artifacts.purpose: Every pass threshold with its justification, author, and review condition.

artifacts.name: Evaluation labor statement
artifacts.purpose: Who ran the evaluation, how long, who covered their duties, and what was skipped when staff could not be spared.

artifacts.name: Projection-to-measurement ledger
artifacts.purpose: Each evaluation projection, its post-deployment measurement, and the review condition connecting them.

example.title: The demo that rehearsed
example.description: A clinical system passes procurement on a scripted demonstration with clean data and a cooperative chart. The stress-test version ingests a chart with two conflicting allergy entries and a stale insurance policy, then issues a corrected biopsy result after staging is complete. The correction requires eleven manual steps across four screens, performed by a physician who is not paid for the time. The scripted demo scored 92. The redline fires on unlogged friction, on the observer's record rather than the committee's summary.

antiPatterns.title: The rehearsed demo
antiPatterns.failure: A vendor-controlled demonstration with clean data and cooperative staff is accepted as evidence the system works.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Live adversarial scenarios with dirty data, run by the personnel who will use the system.
antiPatterns.warning: A demo is a performance. The question is what the system does when the data contradicts itself.

antiPatterns.title: Thresholds without provenance
antiPatterns.failure: Pass marks are set after the first vendor is known, or are cited as if they were measurements.
antiPatterns.counterfactual: Every threshold carries its evidence, its author, and a review condition, recorded before shortlisting.
antiPatterns.warning: Criteria fitted to the answer wanted are the gate-as-rubber-stamp failure of the admission gate.
